h1: Buy vs Rent a Mobile Surveillance Trailer: The Decision Framework
heroSubhead: Renting wins under 24 months. Buying wins beyond 36. The 24-to-36-month window is where capex preference, redeployment needs, and depreciation policy decide it.
body:
This page exists because every procurement conversation eventually lands on this question. We'll give you the math, the qualitative factors, and a clear decision tree.

## The headline math

At the Sky Guard MSU rate ($2,200/mo rental, $38,000 purchase):

| Month | Cumulative Rental Cost | Purchase + Platform/SOC |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | $26,400 | $50,000 ($38K + $12K opex) |
| 18 | $39,600 | $56,000 |
| 24 | $52,800 | $62,000 |
| **30 (break-even)** | **$66,000** | **$68,000** |
| 36 | $79,200 | $74,000 |
| 48 | $105,600 | $86,000 |

Break-even hits around month 30 once you include $1,000/mo of platform + SOC opex that applies to both scenarios. Without SOC and platform costs (just the trailer hardware), break-even moves to month 17.

The pure-hardware view is misleading because almost no one buys a trailer without monitoring. Use the 30-month figure for honest decision-making.

## When to rent

Rent if any of these is true:

- **Project duration is under 24 months** — most construction projects, event security, disaster response, retail seasonal.
- **You need to redeploy** — multi-site portfolios where the trailer follows the active project. Rental terms include redeployment between sites for $500-$1,200 per move.
- **Capex is constrained** — budgets that allocate to opex are easier to approve and don't require depreciation tracking or asset-management overhead.
- **You want bundled service** — deployment, pickup, maintenance, platform, and (optionally) SOC all in one monthly invoice.
- **Single-site duration is uncertain** — if the site might wrap in 8 months or 28 months, rental protects against committing $38K to a uncertain horizon.

## When to buy

Buy if all three are true:

- **Site duration is 36+ months at a fixed location** — long-term industrial sites, permanent commercial parking lots, established utility yards.
- **Capex is available and preferred** — your finance team prefers capitalized assets, depreciation runway, or property-tax-deductible classification.
- **Maintenance overhead is acceptable** — you have facilities staff who can swap a camera or clean a solar panel without a service call.

## The 24-36 month decision

This is the window where the math is close enough that other factors decide it. Use this checklist:

| Question | If yes... | If no... |
|---|---|---|
| Will the trailer move between sites? | Rent | Lean buy |
| Is capex available without offset trade-offs? | Lean buy | Rent |
| Will you replace cameras or hardware within 3 years? | Rent (avoid asset write-down) | Either |
| Is your depreciation period 5+ years? | Buy (longer recovery) | Rent |
| Do you want predictable monthly opex on the security line? | Rent | Buy |
| Is this a one-time project? | Rent | Buy |

## Hidden costs of ownership

Buyers underestimate four things:

1. **Maintenance** — extended warranty is $1,800/year for years 2+. Without it, expect $500-$2,000/year in repair costs.
2. **Storage** — when not deployed, the trailer needs a yard. Some customers absorb this; others pay $100-$300/mo for outdoor storage.
3. **Resale value** — surveillance trailers depreciate 15-25% per year. A $38K trailer is worth roughly $20K-$25K at year 3 and $12K-$18K at year 5.
4. **Tech obsolescence** — cameras, AI models, and cellular standards (4G LTE Sunset is approaching) all evolve. A trailer purchased today is 2-3 years from a meaningful refresh need.

VDS purchases include 1-year warranty standard. Extended warranty ($1,800/yr) covers parts, labor, and cellular module upgrades.

## Cash flow comparison (5-year)

**Rental (Sky Guard with SOC, 5 years):**
- Year 1: $31,188
- Year 2: $31,188
- Year 3: $29,376 (long-term rate kicks in)
- Year 4: $29,376
- Year 5: $29,376
- **Total: $150,504**

**Purchase (Sky Guard with platform + SOC, 5 years):**
- Year 1: $50,196 ($38K + $12.2K opex)
- Year 2: $14,196 (opex only)
- Year 3: $15,996 (opex + warranty)
- Year 4: $15,996
- Year 5: $15,996
- **Total: $112,380**
- Residual asset value: ~$12,000-$15,000

Buying saves about $38K over 5 years and leaves you with a depreciable asset. Renting trades that savings for flexibility, predictability, and no asset-management burden.

## The redeployment factor

Most of our customers ultimately rent because portfolio flexibility outweighs the dollar savings. A construction firm with 12 active projects over 3 years doesn't want to own 4 trailers and idle them between jobs. They rent 6, redeploy as projects start and finish, and pay nothing during the gaps.

If your operation is single-site and the site is permanent, buy. If your operation is portfolio-based, rent.

faq.q: What's the simplest rule of thumb?
faq.a: Under 24 months at a single site, rent. Over 36 months at a single site, buy. In between, decide on capex preference and redeployment need.

faq.q: Can I rent-to-own?
faq.a: Yes. We offer rental-to-purchase conversion where 50% of paid rent (up to 18 months) applies toward the purchase price.

faq.q: What's the depreciation schedule for a purchased trailer?
faq.a: Most accountants use 5-7 year straight-line for surveillance equipment. Your tax advisor will have specifics for your jurisdiction.

faq.q: Are there tax advantages to owning?
faq.a: Section 179 deduction may apply for qualifying business purchases under the federal cap. Consult your accountant.

faq.q: What happens to my purchased trailer at end-of-life?
faq.a: We offer trade-in credit on next-generation models (typically 20-30% of original price at year 5). Otherwise, used surveillance trailers have a small secondary market.

faq.q: Can I lease (not rent) for tax purposes?
faq.a: Yes — we offer 36- and 60-month capital leases through partner financing companies. Monthly cost is similar to rental, with ownership transferring at lease end.

body:
A mobile surveillance trailer is a self-contained tower with cameras, solar power, cellular uplink, and (in most modern configurations) onboard AI analytics. Pricing is driven by five variables: camera count, solar capacity, AI tier, monitoring service, and rental term.

This page covers all five. Numbers are current for 2026.

## Rental pricing (per month)

| Trailer Class | VDS Model | VDS Rate | Industry Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry / construction | Swift Deploy Trailer | $1,500/mo | $1,200-$1,800/mo |
| Mid-tier / multi-camera | Sky Guard MSU | $2,200/mo | $1,800-$2,800/mo |
| Heavy / extended perimeter | Boundary Guard Pro | $1,800/mo | $1,600-$2,400/mo |
| Premium / AI-heavy competitor units | — | — | $2,800-$3,400/mo |

Industry ranges reflect publicly listed rates from LiveView Technologies (LVT), WCCTV, and regional rental fleets. The top of the range ($3,400/mo) is typical for AI-heavy units with bundled monitoring. The bottom ($1,200/mo) is typical for older 4-camera units without analytics.

## Purchase pricing

| VDS Model | Purchase Price | Configuration |
|---|---|---|
| Swift Deploy Trailer | $32,000 | 4 cameras, 800W solar, cellular |
| Sky Guard MSU | $38,000 | 6 cameras, 1.2kW solar, AI analytics, cellular |
| Boundary Guard Pro | $44,000 | 8 cameras + thermal, 1.5kW solar, AI, cellular |
| Custom enterprise build | $50,000-$60,000 | 10+ cameras, redundant power, dual-carrier failover |

Industry purchase prices range $30K (entry units) to $80K+ (custom builds with LiDAR or radar). VDS prices are positioned in the mid-range because we build to NDAA Section 889 specs and use commercial-grade cameras, not consumer hardware.

## What's included in the price

Rental includes hardware, solar power, cellular data, basic VMS access (Standard tier, $39/cam/mo), standard warranty, deployment, and pickup. Purchase includes hardware and 1-year warranty.

## What costs extra

| Line Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Platform Pro tier (advanced AI, analytics, retention) | $69/cam/mo (vs $39/cam/mo Standard) |
| Platform Enterprise tier | Custom |
| 24/7 SOC monitoring | $399/site/mo |
| Extended warranty (purchase only) | $1,800/year |
| Redeployment (moving trailer to new site) | $500-$1,200 per move |
| Custom cellular plan (high-bandwidth) | $50-$150/mo per trailer |
| Site survey (optional) | $0 for VDS — included |

## Annual TCO models

**Construction site, 6 months, rented Sky Guard MSU with SOC:**
- Trailer rental: $2,200 x 6 = $13,200
- Platform (6 cams, Standard): $39 x 6 x 6 = $1,404
- SOC monitoring: $399 x 6 = $2,394
- Deployment/pickup: $0 (included)
- **Total 6-month TCO: $16,998**

**Retail parking lot, 36 months, purchased Sky Guard MSU with SOC:**
- Hardware purchase: $38,000
- Platform (6 cams, Standard, 36 mo): $39 x 6 x 36 = $8,424
- SOC monitoring (36 mo): $399 x 36 = $14,364
- Extended warranty (years 2-3): $1,800 x 2 = $3,600
- **Total 36-month TCO: $64,388 ($1,789/mo amortized)**

**Logistics yard, 12 months, rented Boundary Guard Pro with SOC, Pro platform:**
- Trailer rental: $1,800 x 12 = $21,600
- Platform (8 cams, Pro): $69 x 8 x 12 = $6,624
- SOC monitoring: $399 x 12 = $4,788
- **Total 12-month TCO: $33,012**

## How this compares to a guard line item

A single guard FTE for 24/7 single-site coverage (3 shifts plus overlap) runs $60,000 to $110,000 per year fully loaded. A rented Sky Guard MSU with SOC monitoring runs roughly $33,000 per year. WCCTV publicly cites up to 88% cost reduction vs guards. Our deployments hover in the 75-88% range depending on whether guards are fully replaced or kept for daytime presence.

## Hidden costs to ask about

When evaluating any vendor, ask:
- Are deployment and pickup included or billed separately?
- What is the cellular data overage rate?
- Is the VMS license per-camera or per-trailer?
- Is there a deposit, and what is the return condition?
- What is the response SLA if a trailer goes offline?

Most vendors price these as add-ons. VDS includes deployment, pickup, and unlimited cellular data within the published rate for standard configurations.

body:
Most VDS trailers ship as rentals. The reason is straightforward: construction sites, event security, retail seasonal needs, and disaster response all have variable durations and locations. Owning a trailer that sits idle 4 months a year is worse economics than renting one for the 8 months you need it.

This page covers rental rates by term length, what's included, deposit and lead time, and how redeployment works.

## Rental rates by term

| Term | Swift Deploy | Sky Guard MSU | Boundary Guard Pro |
|---|---|---|---|
| Month-to-month (1-2 mo) | $1,800/mo | $2,600/mo | $2,200/mo |
| Short-term (3-11 mo) | $1,650/mo | $2,400/mo | $2,000/mo |
| Standard (12 mo) | $1,500/mo | $2,200/mo | $1,800/mo |
| Long-term (24+ mo) | $1,350/mo | $1,980/mo | $1,620/mo |

Quarterly billing is available at the 12-month rate. Monthly billing is standard. There's no penalty for ending a rental at the contracted term — extensions or early returns require 30-day notice.

## Per-week and per-quarter math

For short jobs (event security, disaster response, 60-day projects):
- **Per week:** Sky Guard MSU at month-to-month = $2,600/mo ÷ 4.3 weeks = **~$605/week**
- **Per quarter:** Standard 12-month rate prepaid = $2,200 x 3 = **$6,600/quarter**

We don't list a true "per-week" rate because deployment costs make sub-2-week rentals uneconomical for both parties. Minimum rental is 14 days for emergency response, 30 days standard.

## What's included

| Item | Included? |
|---|---|
| Trailer hardware (cameras, solar, tower, batteries) | Yes |
| Cellular data (unlimited) | Yes |
| Platform Standard tier ($39/cam/mo) | Yes |
| Deployment (CONUS) | Yes |
| Pickup at end of term | Yes |
| Routine maintenance | Yes |
| 24/7 hardware support | Yes |

## What costs extra

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Platform Pro tier upgrade | +$30/cam/mo (Standard included, Pro is +) |
| 24/7 SOC monitoring | $399/site/mo |
| Redeployment (move to new site mid-term) | $500-$1,200 |
| Damage waiver (optional) | $75/mo |
| Out-of-region deployment (Alaska, Hawaii) | Quoted |

## Deposit and payment terms

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Security deposit | One month's rent, refundable |
| First month | Due at deployment |
| Net terms (qualified accounts) | Net-30 available |
| Damage deductible (without waiver) | $2,500 |

We don't require a credit check for rentals under 12 months at standard configurations. Larger accounts (multi-trailer, multi-site) typically run on Net-30 with no deposit after a successful first deployment.

## Lead time

| Configuration | Lead Time |
|---|---|
| Standard SKU (Sky Guard, Swift Deploy, Boundary Guard) | 14 days from PO |
| Emergency / disaster response | 48-72 hours (rates apply) |
| Custom configuration | 30-45 days |
| Out-of-state fleet redeployment | 7-10 days |

Standard 14-day lead time is door-to-door from PO to trailer powered on at your site. We keep buffer inventory in regional yards across 12 states for faster turnaround.

## Redeployment between sites

Most of our customers move trailers between sites during a rental. Redeployment fees:
- Same metro area (under 50 miles): $500
- Same state: $800
- Adjacent state: $1,200

There's no per-redeployment charge if you give us 7-day notice and a confirmed new site address. Same-day moves incur a $300 expedite fee on top of the redeployment cost.

## When rental beats purchase

Rent when:
- Site duration is under 24 months
- You need to redeploy across multiple locations
- Capex is unavailable or constrained
- You want predictable opex with bundled service

Buy when:
- Site duration is 36+ months at a fixed location
- You have capex available and prefer ownership
- Your asset depreciation policy favors capitalization

Full break-even math is on [Buy vs Rent](/solutions/buy-vs-rent-mobile-surveillance-trailer). At Sky Guard rates, break-even hits around month 24.

## Insurance and liability

You'll need a Certificate of Insurance naming VDS as additional insured. Most general liability policies cover the trailer for standard perils. Theft and vandalism are covered under our damage waiver ($75/mo) or your insurance, your choice.

$1,500/month vs. $18,000–$36,000/month. The math is straightforward.

Security decisions come down to outcomes and cost. You need reliable coverage that deters crime, documents incidents, and provides usable evidence when something happens. The question isn't whether cameras or guards are "better" — it's which approach delivers the protection you need at a price that makes business sense.

Most property managers discover guard costs exceed their security budget by 300–500%. Meanwhile, remote video monitoring powered by AI analytics and human verification delivers superior documentation, faster response times, and consistent coverage at a fraction of the cost.

## What 24/7 Guard Coverage Actually Costs

The sticker price for security guard services doesn't tell the whole story. To staff a single post 24/7, you need 3–4 guards to cover shifts, breaks, sick days, and vacation coverage. At $28/hour, that's $18,144/month minimum before overtime, holidays, and supervisor costs.

Loaded costs make the real number much higher. Security agencies mark up rates 25–75% to cover their overhead and profit margins. Annual turnover exceeds 100% in most markets, creating constant recruitment and training costs. Workers' compensation insurance adds 30% or more to hourly rates. Holiday and weekend premiums increase costs another 10–25%.

The true cost of 24/7 guard coverage runs $18,000–$36,000/month for a single post. Enterprise clients protecting multiple locations often spend $500,000–$2 million annually on guard services alone.

Base guard wages (3.5 FTE × $28/hr) $18,144 $217,728
Agency markup (35% average) $6,350 $76,205
Holiday/overtime premiums $2,700 $32,400
Turnover/training costs $1,800 $21,600
Total 24/7 guard coverage $28,994 $347,933

Human reliability creates additional problems. Night-shift alertness degradation affects judgment and reaction times. Industry surveys show 30% of security guards admit falling asleep on duty during overnight shifts. Guards follow predictable patrol patterns — theft rings exploit timing gaps and blind spots.

Most importantly, guards cannot document what they didn't see. Without video evidence, incident reports become "he said, she said" disputes that rarely hold up in court or insurance claims.

## VDS Remote Monitoring vs. Security Guards: Head-to-Head

Deterrence method Physical presence Audio challenge + police coordination

VDS remote monitoring combines AI-powered video analytics with human verification through our 24/7 Security Operations Center. When VisionStream AI detects suspicious activity, SOC operators view live footage, issue audio challenges through on-site speakers, and coordinate police response with real-time video evidence.

This hybrid approach — AI detection plus human verification — eliminates the false alarm problem that plagues traditional security systems. Police respond faster when they know the threat is verified and they'll have video evidence to support arrests and prosecutions.

Guards are genuinely necessary for physical ID verification at access points, situations requiring physical intervention, and regulatory requirements specifying on-site personnel. Federal facilities, airports, and high-security manufacturing often mandate human presence for compliance reasons.

## The warehouse cargo theft problem in 2026

Cargo theft has shifted from the highway to the yard. The dominant attack pattern in 2025-2026:

- **Strategic / fictitious pickup** — a thief poses as a legitimate carrier, presents fraudulent paperwork at the gate, hooks up the wrong trailer, and drives off. Loss visibility lags 24-72 hours.
- **Unauthorized trailer hookups** — after-hours bobtail arrival, no scheduled pickup, hookup and exit. The yard fence and a paper gate log are the only controls.
- **Pilferage at the dock** — partial-load theft from staged trailers, often involving inside collusion.
- **Full trailer theft** — bobtail arrives, hooks a loaded trailer, leaves. Often inside knowledge of which trailer carries which load.

CargoNet's 2024 data: average loss per incident exceeded $200,000. Electronics, pharmaceuticals, food, and household goods are the top categories. Recovery rates trail behind heavy equipment.

The gate guard plus a chain-link fence plus paper BOLs is no longer adequate, and shippers are starting to require monitored yard security in vendor contracts.

## How VDS prevents cargo theft at warehouse yards

The defense covers the perimeter, the dock, and the gate, with the SOC as the integration layer:

**Boundary Guard Pro at the yard perimeter.** 500ft of fence-line coverage per unit. Thermal + radar detects fence-line approach (cut-and-enter) and detects bobtail arrival from off-property.

**Swift Deploy with LPR at the dock and gate.** Every truck plate captured under 3 seconds at 95%+ accuracy. Plate logs to AI VisionStream with carrier hot-list lookup. A non-manifested plate triggers SOC review before the trailer hookup.

**AI VisionStream trailer-hookup detection.** The system understands what a trailer hookup looks like — bobtail arrival, backup-to-trailer, fifth-wheel coupling, glad-hand connection, departure. After-hours hookups trigger immediate SOC verification against the dispatch schedule.

**24/7 US SOC.** Operator verifies, audio talk-downs the unauthorized hookup, dispatches LE with live video, and stays on the line. We have stopped trailers mid-exit on multiple occasions.

## The after-hours parking problem in 2026

Open-air lots, structured garages, park-and-ride facilities, and event parking all share the same threat curve: incidents cluster heavily between 10pm and 5am, when the staffed period ends and reactive coverage drops to "review the footage tomorrow." For owners and operators, the costs include:

- **Encampment** — unauthorized overnight occupation, with associated trespass, sanitation, and tenant-relations costs
- **Catalytic converter theft** — covered in detail at [/solutions/auto/catalytic-converter-theft](/solutions/auto/catalytic-converter-theft)

Standard solutions — overnight guards, fixed CCTV with morning review — are expensive (guard run-rate $24,000-$48,000/year per post) and reactive (CCTV records the incident; the response happens days later if at all).

**AI VisionStream time-of-day rules.** Zones automatically arm at the close of business and disarm at the start of the morning shift. ## The festival and event security problem in 2026

The promoter or producer typically owns five overlapping security challenges in parallel:

1. **Build-out period (3-14 days pre-event)** — equipment, AV, staging, vendor inventory arriving and sitting overnight on an unfenced or lightly-fenced site
2. **Ingress / egress** — credentialed vehicle and personnel access at multiple points, with VIP, vendor, talent, crew, and patron categories
3. **In-event perimeter** — fence-line and back-of-house monitoring during operating hours
4. **Vendor zone protection** — high-value vendor inventory (alcohol, merchandise, electronics) targeted during operating hours and overnight
5. **Strike / load-out (1-7 days post-event)** — equipment and staging on the ground while the event is mostly empty

Permanent CCTV is not the answer — the event will be gone in days or weeks. Standard event security (guards + radios + fencing) doesn't produce documentation, doesn't run after hours efficiently, and doesn't capture credentialed vehicle plates at the gate.

## How VDS covers festival and event security

The deployment matches the event timeline:

**Pre-event build-out:** Sky Guard MSU and Swift Deploy units arrive on site within 72 hours of contract. Solar-autonomous — no power tie-in needed. Operational the same day they roll off the trailer.

**Strike / load-out:** Coverage stays in place until the last truck leaves the site. We demobilize on agreed schedule.
